Subject: Skyward Analytics — Post-call recap and proposed next steps

Hi Evelyn — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: get a small proof-of-concept ingesting customer queries into your search/rerank flow and compare cost/latency vs current CPU-based reranker.
- Key integration touchpoints we discussed: SDK setup + auth, request routing for regional failover, structured output/tool-calling for entity extraction, embeddings + reranker pipeline.
- Outstanding technical questions you flagged: chat vs completions semantics for conversation history, tokenization and max_tokens budgeting, behavior of stop sequences across streaming, and how our streaming semantics interact with partial tool outputs.

Next steps we propose: 
1) We’ll send a short technical note with an example request/response schema and a minimal SDK init snippet for your engineers. (Owner: Karthik)
2) Connor will follow up on routing options (single endpoint with region hints vs explicit region endpoints) and recommended retry/fallback config. (Owner: Connor)
3) We’ll attach a mutual action plan with milestone dates and a small sample schema file for your team to review.

If this looks right I’ll loop in Laura for a sample SDK package and share the attachments. Do you have any constraints on max response latency or max tokens for the POC?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifying points before you send the technical note: 

1) Latency: target 200ms p95 for a single rerank request (embedding lookup + model reranker). If that's unrealistic with your hosted plan we can adjust.
2) Token budget: for the POC we want to cap generation to ~256 tokens. How does that interact with streaming? Specifically, if the server streams partial tokens and then stops once 256 total tokens are emitted, do you guarantee any finalization event (e.g., streaming end-of-message marker)?
3) Chat vs completions: our pipeline currently keeps a short chat history (last 3 turns). Do we need the chat API to preserve roles and assistant state, or can we wrap history into a completions-style prompt and still keep structured tool-calls?

Also, can you provide a sample request schema for: 1) embedding generation for batching, 2) a reranker call that accepts a candidate list + metadata, and 3) a tool-calling pattern for extracting entities as JSON? If you can include the small YAML you mentioned that will be perfect.

– Evelyn
Senior Engineering Manager, Skyward Analytics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Skyward Analytics — Post-call recap and proposed next steps (technical note)

Marissa, Connor — drafting the technical note here, answering Evelyn’s bullets inline. Copying Laura for SDK artifacts.

1) Latency: 200ms p95 for embedding + rerank is aggressive for a multi-stage pipeline if you run a large reranker model; for smaller 2–4-layer reranker models we can hit ~150–250ms p95 on our Dedicated pools with batching disabled for single-request low-latency paths. We’ll call out a recommended model/quantization profile.

2) Streaming & token budget: Our streaming closes the websocket/HTTP stream with a deterministic end-frame once the model finishes or the server enforces max_tokens. We expose a finalization event in the SDK (onComplete / end_of_stream) you can rely on to trigger downstream commit logic. If you set max_tokens=256 the runtime counts emitted tokens and will stop the stream at that boundary — partial tool outputs are flushed before the stream close event. Important nuance: if you use prefix caching + batching, token accounting is against generated tokens only, not the cached prefix.

3) Chat vs completions for tool-calling: You can do both. The chat API preserves role metadata (user/system/assistant) and keeps conversation state in the KV cache (recommended if you want efficient incremental generation). For a completions-style single-shot prompt that includes the last N turns, you lose assistant message-level meta but you can still use structured tool-calling by embedding a call spec in the prompt. For Skyward I recommend using the chat API for the POC because you want consistent role preservation and simpler tool-call semantics when invoking entity extraction tools.

Sample schemas (attached as a minimal YAML): 
- embedding_batch: accepts an array of input texts + optional metadata. Returns array of vectors and source ids.
- reranker_call: request contains query_id, candidates[{id, text, metadata}], context_tokens (optional), and a config block {max_tokens, top_k, rerank_mode}. Response is ranked_candidates with scores and optional explanations.
- tool_call (entity extraction): request includes text and a tool schema request for which fields to extract; response is a JSON object matching the provided schema. When streamed, each tool output chunk is JSON-lines; finalization event indicates the object is complete.

I attached the YAML with minimal examples and will let Laura attach a tiny SDK snippet. Connor, can you confirm recommended routing pattern (single endpoint + region hint vs per-region endpoints) and suggested retry config?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sample-request-schema.yaml (yaml)]

Subject: Fwd: Skyward Analytics — Post-call recap and proposed next steps (technical note)

Evelyn — forwarding Karthik’s note and a couple of attachments. Laura is attaching a minimal SDK example below and a quick README for auth. 

— SDK snippet (JS pseudocode) —
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2', retryPolicy: { retries: 2, backoffMs: 100 } });
// chat call with tool-calling schema
const response = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-reranker-small', history: lastThreeTurns, tools: [{ name: 'entity-extract', schemaRef: 'entity_v1' }], max_tokens: 256, stream: true });

Auth/keys: we support standard API key header + optional mTLS for Private deployments and customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. Laura’s README has a short example for local dev vs production.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx, redwood-sample-request-schema.yaml, and SDK README (attached inline). Laura — can you also paste a tiny Python example for their infra team?

Thanks — can we target a 1-week POC start if Skyward can provide a small test dataset and a contact in infra?

Marissa
